title: Per-customer & per-route optimizer: safe recommendation engine and rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a recommendation engine that produces per-customer and per-route batching/caching profiles (including allowlist/denylist and tier controls), plus an automated safe-apply + rollback playbook. The engine should: 1) ingest traffic telemetry and token cost/time distributions; 2) output suggested configs with confidence scores and estimated cost delta; 3) produce a recommended rollout plan (canary cohorts, throttles, fallback models); 4) integrate with Redwood's rollout service to apply changes with automated health checks and reversible rollback hooks. Deliverables: recommender prototype, schema for profiles, health-check predicates, canary orchestration integration, and runbook for on-call and customer success.
acceptance_criteria: Recommender returns per-customer and per-route profiles with confidence and delta estimates
Integration test that applies a profile to a canary cohort and reverses on a simulated latency/error spike
Dashboards display predicted vs actual cost impact over the first 24h post-apply
Playbook documented with exact health-check predicates, alert thresholds, and manual rollback steps
technical_notes: Input features: rolling 1h/24h QPS, median/p95 latency per model/route, token-length distribution, KV cache hit rates, sequence truncation events

Output schema: profile_id, scope (customer|route), recommended_batch_size, cache_ttl_ms, allowlist_tokens_regex[], denylist_routes[], tier_override (gold/silver/bronze), confidence_score (0-1), estimated_cost_delta_pct
Safety checks: require confidence_score >= 0.65 for automatic apply; lower confidence only surface as manual suggestions
Health predicates: 15m rolling change in p95 latency > +20% OR error-rate increase > 0.5% should trigger automated rollback
Rollout strategy: initial 0.5% traffic canary -> 5% -> 20% -> full; each step waits for 30m stable window unless overridden
Fallback: route-aware model variant fallback and region re-routing if canary fails due to capacity
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: Aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latency; what SLO degradation is acceptable per customer tier?
How to encode allowlist/denylist rules without exposing PII from token-level telemetry? Consider hashed token fingerprints.
We can run candidate configs in shadow mode (no-apply) to gather live metrics before an apply, but shadowing doubles telemetry processing cost—budget tradeoff.
Should confidence calibration be global or per-customer? Initial approach: global model with per-segment recalibration later.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2w): data pipeline to aggregate per-route/customer telemetry + offline cost-model training
Phase 2 (3w): recommender service that emits profiles and UI API endpoints
Phase 3 (2w): integrate with rollout orchestration and implement automated health checks
Phase 4 (1w): build dashboards and finalize runbook; run internal canary against non-prod tenants
Phase 5 (cont): monitor, iterate, extend to Dedicated/Private deployment configs
